newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa govt opposes iron ore pipe through Kruger.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa govt opposes iron ore pipe through Kruger.

text.p: South Africa's Environment Minister Pallo Jordan said on Friday he was opposed to piping iron ore slurry through the Kruger National Park, the country's premier wildlife area and a prime tourist attraction.

The state-owned Industrial Development Corporation (IDC) had proposed three alternatives routes for a pipeline to ship magnetite from Phalaborwa to Maputo in neighbouring Mozambique, where it would feed a proposed 5.2 billion rand iron ore reduction plant.
Two of the routes for the slurry pipeline would transgress the Kruger which Jordan said would pose a "very serious threat to the integrity of the park".
The possibility of magnetite being piped to Mozambique through the Kruger had already caused an outcry among conservationists.
Magnetite is waste produced from copper operations at Phalaborwa on the western edge of the park and has been accumulating in stockpiles for more than 30 years.

The suggested iron ore plant would provide an ideal anchor client for Mozambique's Pande gas field near Inhassorro, about 600 km northeast of Maputo, which the Mozambican government and American energy firm Enron Corp plan to develop.
